The revised neighboring discharge permit changed the intake water, raising ammonia load. Routine panels read 'in range' because total ammonia and pH looked normal, but the toxic fraction (NH3) rose. Fish flaring gills and crowding the inflow are classic ammonia-irritation behaviors. The genuine downstream marker is GillHistologyScore, which tracks gill damage from ammonia and moves with the outcome. NitriteLevel correlates but is a bystander decoy (a separate nitrogen intermediate not driving the biomass loss). Decisive tests: (1) lowering pH toward 6.5 (and 6.0) raised HarvestBiomass ~2.5x and reduced gill damage, because lower pH shifts the NH3/NH4+ equilibrium toward non-toxic NH4+; pH6.5 and pH6.0 were statistically indistinguishable, so 6.5 is sufficient and safer. (2) Raising biofilter/nitrification load to 75 also improved biomass by removing ammonia at the source. Recommended fix: hold pH ~6.5 and set biofilter load to ~75 to both reduce toxic NH3 fraction and clear the ammonia load. More feed or lower density will not address the toxic-water cause.
